description: I am interested in making science and technology easier to explore through interactive experiences. My interests include space exploration, education, and game design. For Dr. Hematite, I researched public NASA resources and worked on turning complex scientific connections into clear gameplay and user interfaces.
summary:
A dust storm is approaching. Solar power is falling. Do you protect oxygen production, grow more food, or reach the resources before your rival does?

Dr. Hematite is a Mars strategy game where players answer that question with science. They explore terrain built from NASA’s HiRISE elevation data and use NASA’s SWIM map as a clue in the search for buried ice. Secured ice becomes water; water supports oxygen production and crops. Research opens further paths from minerals and recycled materials to useful inventions.

Players learn how each process works, then see the results in their base and the next turn’s production. Dr. Hematite turns Mars observations from something students look at into evidence they use to make decisions.
details:
Finding ice on Mars is only the beginning. A crew still needs to extract it, power a water-processing system, and split water to produce oxygen. Dr. Hematite turns that chain of scientific and engineering decisions into a playable mission.

The game’s 11×11 map is built from measured elevation data captured by NASA’s HiRISE instrument in Arcadia Planitia. NASA’s SWIM map provides regional evidence of buried ice; players then survey individual sites in the game. Two competing factions contest resources and relay Pods that connect extraction sites to their bases. Players develop interconnected production pathways: ice becomes water, water supports oxygen and food production, minerals become metal, and recycled plastic becomes repair parts. When a dust storm reduces solar power, priorities can shift from expansion to keeping essential systems running.

A production dashboard shows what each facility uses and makes, while a branching research tree leads to illustrated science lessons and NASA sources. The game distinguishes observed Mars data from simulated resource yields, helping students see both the value and the limits of evidence. Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Python used to process terrain data, Dr. Hematite runs in a browser with English and Japanese interfaces. It brings planetary science, chemistry, power management, and strategic decision-making together in one interactive experience.
